name: v0.4.9: dual control surfaces (OSC relay), gyro indicator fix, autopilot fallback clock + column advance
body:
## v0.4.9: dual control surfaces (OSC relay), gyro indicator fix, autopilot fallback clock + column advance

Pre-show release. The Resolume comp, Wire patches, TouchOSC patches, and shortcut presets travel separately — this installer carries the bridge plus factory engine configs only.

### What changed

- **OSC relay — run two TouchOSC surfaces at once.** Resolume Arena's OSC output accepts exactly **one** target (`Preferences/osc.xml` has a single `<Output>` element; this is a format limitation, not a UI one), which made a second control surface impossible. The bridge now carries a UDP fan-out: point Resolume at the bridge on localhost and it re-sends every datagram to every configured destination. A Steam Deck and an iPad can now both run TouchOSC against the same composition, each on its own page, with full state feedback.

  It forwards **raw bytes and never parses OSC**. Arena sends with `sendBundles="1"`, so the wire carries `#bundle` packets with timetags plus OSC type `r` packed colors — forwarding verbatim is what makes bundles, colors, and any future Resolume message type survive intact.

  This is core receiver infrastructure, deliberately **not** an engine: engines have a per-preset on/off toggle, and one left off here would silently kill OSC feedback to every surface at once, mid-show, with no visible symptom.

  Live-show hardening: separate receive/send sockets with per-destination error isolation, so one unreachable surface (a sleeping iPad) can never starve the other; Windows `SIO_UDP_CONNRESET` disabled, because an ICMP Port Unreachable otherwise fails the *next* socket call with `WSAECONNRESET` and would kill the relay thread when a surface drops off Wi-Fi; a missing config file means "no relay", so installs that never configure one behave exactly as before; and a bind failure is logged and swallowed, because losing OSC feedback must never stop the bridge delivering MIDI.

- **TouchOSC gyro indicator revived.** It had been dead since analog gyro replaced the digital gyro notes. Three things combined: every layer publisher starts `UNKNOWN`; the toggle handler early-returns on `UNKNOWN`; and the gyro publisher's only ground-truth actions (`GYRO_FORWARD`/`GYRO_BACKWARD`) were dropped from every preset when analog gyro landed. So it was pinned at `UNKNOWN` forever and its layer CC was never published — "ignore the toggle until ground truth arrives" had quietly become "ignore the toggle forever". The gyro publisher is now seeded to layer 1 (gyro off, matching deck boot). A second half of the same bug is also fixed: a preset hot-swap rebuilt the publishers without re-seeding, which would have killed the indicator again.

- **Autopilot: fallback clock for shows without Pulse.** Every cycle event hung off the MIDI clock, so a rig with no Pulse got no beats at all and autopilot did nothing. There is now a free-running wall-clock beat generator (default **128 BPM**) that takes over after 2 s of MIDI-clock silence and stands down the instant a real tick lands, so Pulse always wins and the two can never both drive the beat. Catch-up is capped so waking from a stall can't machine-gun clip triggers into Resolume. `status()` reports `clock_source` so it's visible which clock is driving.

- **Autopilot: per-group column advance.** Autopilot cycled layers but never changed columns. On cycle wrap it now steps the channel's layer group to its next column, giving the intended loop: **layer 1 → 2 → 3 → (column advance + back to layer 1) → repeat**. Uses `/composition/groups/N/connectnextcolumn`, the same path Resolume's own MIDI shortcut binds for manual column triggers. Configured per channel via `group` and `column_advance`.

- **`scripts/keycode_watch.py` — deck-side keycode diagnostic.** The sender silently drops unmapped X11 keycodes with no log line, which makes three very different Steam Input failures look identical from the Windows side: an action set that never switched, one that switched to unbound keys, and one that sent nothing. This prints every raw keycode with its binding (or `*** UNMAPPED ***`). It reuses the sender's own XI2 listener and is safe to run alongside it, since XI2 raw events are delivered to every client that selects for them.

### Not a code change, but worth recording

A long-standing "the SELECT/START layer buttons don't work" symptom was traced with the new keycode watcher to the **Steam Input layout**, not the bridge. Three faults in the layout: activation used *Hold* Action Set Layer (so the layer died on button release), the two layer commands sat on the **swapped** buttons, and both *Remove* commands pointed at the opposite layer so a toggle could never latch. The bridge's SELECT/START mapping was correct throughout and needed no change.

### How to upgrade

Run the installer (it closes a running receiver automatically).

**The installer does not ship `config/osc_relay.json`** — copy it into the install's `config/` by hand to enable the relay. No launch-argument change is needed; the relay defaults to `<map dir>/osc_relay.json`. Destination ports are per-device (the two surfaces here receive on 7002 and 7001), so neither `.tosc` patch needs editing.

As always, engine configs and presets are **not** overwritten on upgrade: the installer preserves user tuning (`onlyifdoesntexist`), and user `config/engines/*.json` files are not shipped at all (only `config/engines.factory/*.json`). New factory keys — including autopilot's `fallback_clock`, `group`, and `column_advance` — only apply if you have no user override for that engine type.

**Install gotcha (re-confirmed this release):** a tray can come up on the *pre-sync* config, and the single-instance mutex then makes a second launch exit silently, so the running instance never sees your synced config. Stop **all** trays, then start **one** fresh *after* the config sync.

### Post-install

Autopilot channel state (per-layer enables and MODE) lives only in bridge memory and is seeded by CCs from the Wire patch, so **every restart zeroes it** — nudge the autopilot layer buttons and the MODE selector after installing, or autopilot will sit idle while TouchOSC still displays the old settings. Set the FX channel's MODE to LINEAR if you want FX advancing clips (FX is ungrouped, so it steps clips on its own layer rather than columns).

### Tests

648 tests green (2 pre-existing Linux-only import errors, 1 skip).
